Time to reach a level of the asymptote

Source: R/timeto.R
timeto.Rd

Estimates the times at which growth curves reach a percentage of their asymptote, or a given response, with standard errors by the delta method and automatic differentiation.

Usage

timeto(
  x,
  level = 50,
  curves = NULL,
  newdata = NULL,
  random = TRUE,
  residual = FALSE,
  type = c("relative", "absolute")
)

Arguments

x

A gcTMB object, the result of gcTMB.

level

Numeric vector. Levels in percent of the asymptote b1, between 0 and 100 (default 50): the time at which the curve reaches p percent of b1, e.g. b2 + b3 log(p/(100 - p)) for the logistic curve, b2 - b3 log(-log(p/100)) for gompertz, and b2 (p/(100 - p))^(1/b3) for hill. For the logistic, normal and hill curves without truncation, the time of 50 percent is b2. For a curve truncated at the threshold b4 (the default of gcTMB), the levels are of the truncated curve, the time at which the curve f without truncation reaches f(b4) + p/100 (b1 - f(b4)). For the chapmanrichards and korf curves, the levels are of the growth above the intercept b4, and for preecebaines of the adult height b1. For type="absolute", values of the response; the linear model, which has no asymptote, has only these.

curves

Numeric matrix, list of matrices, or NULL. Linear functions to identify the parameters of the growth curve, with 5 rows (b1-b5) and one column for each model coefficient, or a list of such matrices. If curves and newdata are both NULL (default), the identity matrix, for models without covariates in fform. Each matrix is paired with an entry of level.

newdata

Data frame or NULL. The values of the covariates in fform, one row for each growth curve, as an alternative to curves; the time is not needed. NULL (default) to use curves. With grouping variables of the random effects, the curves of fitted groups, see Details. The times are computed at each entry of level for each row, named by the covariate and group values (or by the row names of newdata, if set).

random

Logical. If TRUE, the times of rows of newdata with fitted groups are conditional on their random effects, and for the other random effect terms, the variance-covariance matrix of the random effects is included in the standard error estimation. If FALSE, the times are for the population curves.

residual

Logical. If TRUE, the residual variance is included in the standard error estimation (gaussian family only)

type

Character string. "relative" (default) for levels relative to the asymptote, or "absolute" for the times at which the curves reach the responses in level, on the scale of the response (proportions for binomial, beta-binomial and beta). Responses outside the range of a curve, between zero and the asymptote, give NA, with a warning.

Value

A timetoTMB object: a list with the estimated times (coef), their covariance matrix (vcov), and what confint and profile need. The times are named by the level, e.g. 10% (relative) or y=10 (absolute), followed by the name of the curve for curves from newdata or named curves, e.g. 10%:trt=0.1; several unnamed curves are numbered.

Details

Without random effects, or with random=FALSE, the times are those of the population curves, with all random effects at zero, and their standard errors include the uncertainty of the fixed effects only. With random=TRUE, the standard errors also include the variance of the random effects, the variation of the time between groups.

If a row of newdata gives a level of a grouping factor that is in the fitted data, the time of that row is for the curve of the group, with its predicted random effects (the conditional modes), as in predict.gcTMB. These are shrunken towards the population curve, more so for groups with few observations. Their standard errors include the uncertainty of the fixed effects and the prediction error of the random effects, from the joint precision matrix of sdreport. Random effect terms without a grouping variable in newdata, or with a level that is not in the fitted data, are treated as above. Profile intervals are not available for the times of fitted groups, see confint.timetoTMB.

See also

confint.timetoTMB for confidence intervals, profile.timetoTMB

Examples

fit <- gcTMB(Height ~ DAS, data=FabaHeights25, model="logistic")
# days after sowing at which the plants reach 10%, 50% and 90% of their final height
tt <- timeto(fit, level=c(10, 50, 90))
tt
#> Times to reach the percentages of the asymptote:
#> 
#>     Estimate Std.Error
#> 10%     10.8     0.423
#> 50%     32.9     0.911
#> 90%     60.3     2.743
confint(tt)
#> Computing profile confidence intervals ...
#>        2.5 %   97.5 %
#> 10% 10.02726 11.69745
#> 50% 31.32441 35.05932
#> 90% 55.61967 66.81695
# the day at which they reach a height of 50
timeto(fit, level=50, type="absolute")
#> Times to reach the responses:
#> 
#>      Estimate Std.Error
#> y=50     28.8     0.336

# a curve for each treatment level
FabaHeights25$trt <- factor(FabaHeights25$Treatment)
fit2 <- gcTMB(Height ~ DAS, fform=b1 + b2 ~ trt, data=FabaHeights25)
timeto(fit2, level=90, newdata=data.frame(trt=levels(FabaHeights25$trt)))
#> Times to reach the percentages of the asymptote:
#> 
#>             Estimate Std.Error
#> 90%:trt=0.1     60.2      2.90
#> 90%:trt=0.3     59.0      2.82
#> 90%:trt=0.5     60.7      2.92
#> 90%:trt=0.6     61.2      2.96
#> 90%:trt=0.8     61.4      2.98
